source: Authored from the real part layout of the supplied CAD model (bottom-up build order). It is not the manufacturer's procedure: fastener sizes, torques, wiring and adjustment steps are not documented. Disassembly runs the same steps in reverse.

steps.title: Base plate and handles
steps.assemble: Place the base plate on a flat bench and fit the carry handles at both ends.
steps.disassemble: Remove the carry handles. The base plate is the last part left.
steps.explanation: The base plate is the foundation for the frame and all electrical equipment.

steps.title: DIN rails and electrical modules
steps.assemble: Screw the two DIN rails to the base. Clip on the power supply, the two DIN modules, the terminal blocks and the circuit breaker.
steps.disassemble: Release each module's DIN clip with a flat screwdriver and tilt it off the rail, then unscrew the rails.
steps.explanation: Standard 35 mm DIN rail lets modules be clipped on and off without tools other than a screwdriver for the clip and terminals.

steps.title: Wiring ducts
steps.assemble: Fit the slotted wiring ducts along the base between the frame area and the electrics.
steps.disassemble: Remove the duct covers and lift out the wiring ducts.
steps.explanation: Ducts route and protect the cables to the motor, sensors and solenoid.

steps.title: Servo drive
steps.assemble: Stand the servo drive upright at the side of the base and secure its mounting screw.
steps.disassemble: Unplug the drive cables, remove the mounting screw and lift the servo drive away.
steps.explanation: The servo drive powers and controls the servo motor that indexes the table.

steps.title: Frame legs and cross beams
steps.assemble: Stand the four legs on the base, fit the cross beams between them and tighten the frame screws.
steps.disassemble: Loosen the frame screws, remove the cross beams and lift off the legs.
steps.explanation: The square frame raises the working surface and leaves room for the drive train.

steps.title: Motor mount plate and servo motor
steps.assemble: Fit the motor mount plate across the frame, then fix the servo motor beneath it with its shaft pointing up.
steps.disassemble: Support the servo motor, remove its screws and lower it out, then remove the motor mount plate.
steps.explanation: The motor must sit exactly under the table axis so the coupling runs true.

steps.title: Support bar, drive supports and coupling
steps.assemble: Fit the support bridge bar, the four drive supports and the top plate brackets, then clamp the shaft coupling onto the motor shaft.
steps.disassemble: Loosen the coupling clamp, then remove the brackets, drive supports and support bar.
steps.explanation: These parts hold the drive train in line and connect the motor shaft to the disc.

steps.title: Inductive sensors
steps.assemble: Mount the two cylindrical inductive sensors under the top-plate level and set their gap to the target.
steps.disassemble: Unplug the sensor cables and remove the two inductive sensors.
steps.explanation: Inductive sensors detect metal without contact. Their exact targets need confirmation on the kit.

steps.title: Top plate
steps.assemble: Lower the top plate onto the frame around the coupling and tighten its screws evenly.
steps.disassemble: Remove the top plate screws and lift the top plate straight up.
steps.explanation: The top plate is the common reference surface for the disc and all four stations.

steps.title: Indexing disc
steps.assemble: Seat the indexing disc on the coupling hub in the centre opening of the top plate.
steps.disassemble: Lift the indexing disc off the hub.
steps.explanation: The disc carries the product between stations in quarter-turn steps.

steps.title: Station 1 — RFID head
steps.assemble: Fix the RFID bracket to the top plate and mount the RFID head on it, aimed at the disc rim.
steps.disassemble: Unplug the RFID cable, remove the RFID head and then its bracket.
steps.explanation: Station 1 identifies the product by reading and writing its RFID tag.

steps.title: Station 2 — distance sensor
steps.assemble: Fix the slotted bracket with its thumb screws and mount the distance sensor above the disc rim.
steps.disassemble: Unplug the sensor cable, remove the distance sensor and loosen the thumb screws to free the bracket.
steps.explanation: Station 2 measures the product height or distance to verify its dimensions.

steps.title: Station 3 — camera bridge and camera
steps.assemble: Bolt the camera bridge over the disc rim and fit the USB camera under its top, looking down.
steps.disassemble: Unplug the USB cable, remove the camera and unbolt the camera bridge.
steps.explanation: Station 3 inspects the product with image processing.

steps.title: Station 4 — solenoid
steps.assemble: Mount the linear solenoid on the top plate with its pusher facing the disc rim.
steps.disassemble: Disconnect the solenoid wires and remove the solenoid with its pusher.
steps.explanation: Station 4 pushes the product when the PLC switches the solenoid output.

steps.title: Test product
steps.assemble: Place the tagged test product in its pocket on the disc at station 1.
steps.disassemble: Lift the test product off the disc.
steps.explanation: The kit is ready: the product will be identified, measured, inspected and sorted.
